title: Understand source/admission refusals without resetting access or replaying work
goal: Classify local source/admission refusals and preserve safe context without suggesting unapproved retries or security workarounds.
prerequisites: Internal source-only local preview, not an installed or production inspection. Codes are not asserted to appear in current public v0.1.21 or any uninspected session.

Supplemental to the historical local-source-refusals guide. Fourteen of its15recorded keys remain unchanged; the admitted-app-ai contextual route changed after the approved policy-freshness repair. Its old hash is not current integrity proof.
No UI-control inventory is established here. Proposed IDs label documentation state/recovery families, not actual buttons, stable mounted help metadata or permission keys.
permissions: Being authenticated, admin or connected is not a substitute for verified tenant/repository source authority or funded AI admission. A public or private route has its own current checks.
No reconnect, new consent, tenant/header fabrication, environment flag, provider switch, credit purchase, secret disclosure or automatic retry is authorized by these explanations.
Genuine independent human decisions, one-attempt limits and unknown effects remain mandatory in supported workflows. Documentation cannot approve or replay them.

steps.instruction: refusal-recovery.identify: Record the exact safe code/status, feature and version without resubmitting a request.
steps.expectedState: These are source-specific refusal states, not proof of a failed deployment or that every connector is broken. Use only an existing safe correlation/reference if actually supplied; never invent one.

steps.instruction: refusal-recovery.tenant-source: If the inspected local workflow reports github.tenant_source_required (412), preserve the context and use only an independently supported scoped workflow.
steps.expectedState: The legacy ambient GitHub source lacks verified workspace ownership. Signed-in/admin identity, a server credential, another organization name or a source label cannot supply that missing binding.

steps.instruction: refusal-recovery.preview: Keep synthetic preview or disabled observations separate from successful live discovery.
steps.expectedState: A preview is not restored authority or tenant isolation proof. Audit-start entries can precede refusal and do not prove a provider scan occurred.

steps.instruction: refusal-recovery.public-admission: If the local website assistant reports ai.public_admission_unavailable (503), use available documentation/help rather than repeatedly submitting.
steps.expectedState: This anonymous route lacks a verified usage owner/allowance/admission; its fixed gate precedes body/configuration/prompt/inference processing in the inspected source.

steps.instruction: refusal-recovery.rate-limit: Distinguish an earlier anonymous HTTP429 from the missing-admission503.
steps.expectedState: The existing IP limiter runs first. Waiting does not create funding or permission, and no automatic retry/fallback is authorized.

steps.instruction: refusal-recovery.app-text: Treat the authenticated app text route as a separate workflow with its own current policy, scope, request and budget checks.
steps.expectedState: The later approved repair supplies server-pinned Gateway model policy to admission; shared-row policy checks occur at durable claim and immediately before supported dispatch. This does not restore anonymous assistance or certify all AI paths.

steps.instruction: refusal-recovery.unknown: Preserve unknown or consumed action history while seeking support.
steps.expectedState: Neither refusal provides permission to reset consent, widen a token, swap accounts, change settings, resend an action or infer that no earlier effect occurred.

steps.instruction: refusal-recovery.handoff: Use the supported help route with a safe minimal version/code description.
steps.expectedState: Do not disclose credentials, private prompts, repository screenshots or customer data. This article sends no message and promises no support resolution or current destination health.

steps.instruction: refusal-recovery.freshness: Before relying on this description, match the exact supported version and source evidence; escalate when absent.
steps.expectedState: The historical guide ledger has one stale contextual AI-handler hash. It remains history; the new article binds the current route/helpers explicitly. No source hash or schema pass grants customer eligibility or execution authority.

expectedOutcome: Understand which missing boundary the exact local code describes and retain minimal safe evidence for a supported next step; no restored discovery, funded inference or operational success is inferred.
limitations: The original GitHub ambient-source gate and anonymous assistant gate are unchanged by this authoring. The changed app handler adds textPolicy to admitAIText; current helper semantics come from separately pinned current source, not blindly rebinding the old ledger.

Logical current-policy checks and one-use model binding do not cancel an already sent SDK request, prove atomic physical-wire revocation, qualify every direct/extraction/quoted caller or establish full issuer/custody/fleet coverage.
Usage/SDK/write/preparation uncertainty can retain held capacity. No automatic refund, retry, second-provider dispatch or useful qualified price/quote is established.
Existing local synthetic/compiled-negative and database evidence has its own source scope; no source inspection here is a real HTTP/provider/AI/production/native test.
Exact mounted screens, current connection health, true customer account access, authentic media, human editorial approval and customer/retrieval acceptance remain open.
recovery: Record exact code/version and an existing safe reference when available. Preserve the originating task/action and use qualified supported help, not a guessed identifier or new account.
Do not buy credits or change models expecting the anonymous gate to lift. Missing public funding design differs from authenticated workspace credit exhaustion.

Do not interpret this selected GitHub discovery refusal as failure of all GitHub installation/repository operations or unrelated integrations. Every separate workflow still needs current permission/readback.

If source/version/approved guidance is missing or drifted, refuse/escalate. Historical records must remain intact until explicit re-review; never automatically rewrite source hashes or extend expired approvals.
